messages:
cleo: Hey — hitting a weird Windows shortcut UX: redwoodctl launched from a desktop shortcut ignores `--profile` and falls back to the default profile. localserve starts with prod creds 😬
aj: Huh. can you paste the shortcut Target and a short debug run? e.g. `redwoodctl localserve --profile dev --debug`
cleo: Shortcut target is: `\"C:\\Program Files\\Redwood\\redwoodctl.exe\" localserve --profile dev`
cleo: Debug snippet: `reading profile from C:\\Users\\cleo\\AppData\\Roaming\\Redwood\\profiles\\default.json` even though flag present
samir: My guess: when launched from explorer the working dir and environment differ, so the binary might resolve config from a different location or elevation context. Do you have the MSI installed for all users?
cleo: Yup MSI system-wide install. Works fine when run from cmd or PowerShell though. Only broken via the shortcut double-click. :thinking_face: 
aj: That matches a permission/elevation race. Shortcuts can be set to run as admin or with a different Start In. Can you check the shortcut Properties -> Advanced -> "Run as administrator"? If set, it might switch to the system profile.
cleo: Not set. Start In is blank. I tried adding `--profile dev` to the Target and still same result.
maria: I can repro on Win11 with a machine-wide install. Repro steps: create shortcut to installed redwoodctl, add arg `localserve --profile staging`, double-click = wrong profile. Running from PS works. Logging shows it reads from `C:\\Windows\\System32\\config\\systemprofile\\\\.redwood` path for some reads.
devex-bot: New bug created: RDW-UX-1198 — redwoodctl desktop shortcut ignores CLI profile when installed system-wide. Labels: windows, cli, high-pri. Link: https://redwood.internal/issue/RDW-UX-1198
aj: Temporary workaround: set env var in the shortcut target so config resolves correctly. Use a wrapper cmd like:
```
@echo off
set REDWOODCTL_PROFILE=dev
cd /d %USERPROFILE%
"C:\\Program Files\\Redwood\\redwoodctl.exe" localserve --profile dev --debug
```
aj: Alternatively install per-user instead of system-wide. We'll fix binary config resolution so it always respects explicit `--profile` even when launched from different user contexts.
cleo: Workaround works for me, thanks! Can you add a note to the Windows install docs until the fix ships?
maria: Adding doc patch now. PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/987
samir: I'll take the bug and investigate why argv parsing falls back to systemprofile. Likely an early config init uses HOMEDRIVE/HOME fallback before flags parsed in some elevated path.
cleo: Thanks team. Leaving logs here in case it's useful:
```
[2024-03-11T14:02:10Z] args: ["C:\\Program Files\\Redwood\\redwoodctl.exe", "localserve", "--profile", "dev"]
[2024-03-11T14:02:10Z] open config: C:\\Windows\\System32\\config\\systemprofile\\AppData\\Roaming\\Redwood\\profiles\\default.json
```
aj: Nice logs. Samir if you need a repro VM I can share mine.
samir: Please do. I'll try to repro with and without elevation and check where the effective USERPROFILE/HOME is computed. Ty everyone. :thumbsup:
cleo: Cheers — marking as resolved after fix lands.
